title: Inspection of I/O Operations from System Call Traces using Directly-Follows-Graph
problem: Identifying differences in I/O behavior between multiple programs through system call inspection is challenging because typical programs issue large numbers of I/O requests to the operating system. Analyzing raw traces becomes intractable due to their size and complexity.
motivation: Understanding I/O behavior patterns and differences across programs and configurations is critical for performance optimization, system tuning, and comparative program analysis in HPC environments.
method: The methodology synthesizes I/O system call traces into Directly-Follows-Graphs (DFG), a directed graph representation where nodes are I/O operations and edges represent temporal ordering. Using DFGs, the authors present a comparison technique that identifies behavioral differences between traces from different programs or configurations. The approach is applied to the IOR benchmark under different file output options and software interfaces to analyze file access contention patterns.
key_novelty: Using Directly-Follows-Graph representation to synthesize and compare I/O system call traces for systematic identification of behavioral differences.
contributions: Methodology to synthesize I/O system call traces into DFGs for scalable analysis
Trace comparison technique based on DFG structure to identify I/O behavioral differences
Application to IOR benchmark demonstrating practical utility
Analysis revealing file access contention patterns under different configurations

metrics.other: I/O behavior patterns, file access contention analysis

primary_theme: I/O behavior characterization through system call trace analysis
